summary: A fresh deployment that never set a reply-timeout budget could refuse to start; the default budget now has room for the stages that share it.
details: One conversation's reply slot is held by more than one stage, and a start-up check refuses to run if their timeouts add up to more than the budget — deliberately, so an impossible budget is found while the operator is still holding the config file rather than during a live conversation.

The default budget was exactly the sum of the stages that existed when it was written, with nothing left over. Adding the correction loop's own timeout put the default sum over the default budget, so a deployment that had never set the value would refuse to start.
The default budget is now larger than the default sum, so the next stage to join the slot fails that check with a number to reason about rather than making every unconfigured deployment fail to boot.
Deployments that set the budget explicitly are unaffected.
